run.question: I'm investigating an error in trace TRACE-ERR-X9K2M. Check Elasticsearch and tell me which service failed and what the error was.

report.summary: The trace identifier TRACE-ERR-X9K2M exists only in the Elasticsearch index app-245-apm-traces (the only index matching *), which holds 22 documents in the sampled hour 2026-11-23T16:10:38Z–17:10:38Z. Two of those documents belong to TRACE-ERR-X9K2M. The error is recorded on the span of service payment-gateway, operation authenticate_payment: error.type ConnectionTimeout and error.message 'Authentication service timeout - error code AUTH-4729', http.status_code 503, duration_ms 5180. Its stack trace shows the payment_gateway application awaiting self.http_client.post(auth_url, json=payload, timeout=5.0) in /app/payment_gateway/clients/auth_client.py line 201, i.e. payment-gateway timed out calling an authentication service. The parent span of that span (parent_span_id span-gw-err) belongs to service api-gateway, operation POST /api/payment, and its own document also carries http.status_code 503 with duration_ms 5234, so the api-gateway request that fronted this call failed as well. The other 20 documents in the window are TRACE-OK-* records with http.status_code 200 for api-gateway POST /api/payment and payment-service process_payment, so those two series show no error in the sample. The service that payment-gateway called (an authentication service at auth_url) produced no document in this index, and no workload of that name exists in the cluster, so its own state is not observable here; the deepest cause therefore remains unconfirmed and no root-cause object can be named. Jaeger and Prometheus were unreachable (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE) during this Run, so neither span data nor metric/label data from those sources could be checked.

claims.text: The Elasticsearch index app-245-apm-traces maps the fields trace_id, service, operation, span_id, parent_span_id, duration_ms, error.message, error.type, error.stack_trace and http.status_code, and a search across its documents in the window 2026-11-23T16:10:38Z–17:10:38Z returned 22 documents (total 22, none omitted) whose service values are payment-gateway, api-gateway and payment-service.

Document c55jCaIBRlXO9qICQK31 in app-245-apm-traces (@timestamp 2026-11-23T17:09:00.050Z, trace_id TRACE-ERR-X9K2M) is the span of service payment-gateway, operation authenticate_payment, span_id span-pay-err, parent_span_id span-gw-err, duration_ms 5180, http.status_code 503, with error.type ConnectionTimeout and error.message exactly 'Authentication service timeout - error code AUTH-4729'.

The error.stack_trace on that payment-gateway span shows the failure inside /app/payment_gateway/handlers/payment_handler.py (process_payment) calling /app/payment_gateway/clients/auth_client.py line 201 authenticate(), which awaits self.http_client.post(auth_url, json=payload, timeout=5.0); the observed span duration of 5180 ms is consistent with that 5.0 s client timeout being exceeded.

Document cp5jCaIBRlXO9qICQK31 (@timestamp 2026-11-23T17:09:00Z, trace_id TRACE-ERR-X9K2M) is the span of service api-gateway, operation POST /api/payment, span_id span-gw-err, duration_ms 5234 and http.status_code 503; its span_id matches the parent_span_id of the payment-gateway error span, so per the supplied parent reference api-gateway's POST /api/payment is the parent of payment-gateway's authenticate_payment.

The remaining 20 returned documents in the same window are TRACE-OK-* traces (16:55:00Z–17:04:00Z) in which service api-gateway operation POST /api/payment has http.status_code 200, duration_ms 245, and service payment-service operation process_payment has http.status_code 200, duration_ms 180; no error field or non-200 status appears on those documents.

The cluster's deployment list at query time contains 24 deployments, all with available replicas equal to replicas, and includes none named payment-gateway, api-gateway or auth; the otel-demo namespace contains payment, frontend, frontend-proxy, checkout, jaeger, flagd and other otel-demo components, so the trace's service identities do not correspond to workloads observable in this cluster.

The proximate cause of the failure is an unresponsive or unreachable authentication service: payment-gateway's outbound HTTP call to auth_url exceeded the configured 5.0 s timeout, producing ConnectionTimeout and a 503 surfaced through api-gateway's POST /api/payment. This is a hypothesis because no document in app-245-apm-traces carries the authentication service as its service identity and no workload of that name exists in the cluster, so the dependency's own error/latency evidence was not observed.

Rejected: an api-gateway-internal fault as the origin. The api-gateway span carries 503 only as the status it returned for POST /api/payment, while the error object (error.type ConnectionTimeout, error.message 'Authentication service timeout - error code AUTH-4729') and the outbound auth_client call site are on the child payment-gateway span; api-gateway's same operation returned 200 in the 20 TRACE-OK-* documents of the same window.

Rejected: payment-service as the failing service. The service named payment-service appears only as operation process_payment with http.status_code 200 and duration_ms 180 in the TRACE-OK-* documents; the failing span belongs to the differently named service payment-gateway, and no document ties payment-service to trace TRACE-ERR-X9K2M.

Advisory: verify the authentication service behind auth_url (DNS/endpoint reachability, its own p99 latency versus payment-gateway's 5.0 s client timeout) and review payment-gateway's auth_client timeout/retry settings; when Jaeger and Prometheus are reachable again, check service_name label series for an auth service and payment-gateway error counts to confirm the dependency failure.

gaps: Jaeger was unreachable in this Run: traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE on two attempts, so no span-level confirmation of the trace or of a call edge beyond the supplied parent_span_id could be obtained.

traces_query_trace_by_id for 'TRACE-ERR-X9K2M' returned INVALID_PARAMS (the value is not a valid hexadecimal trace ID), so the trace was found only through the trace_id field of app-245-apm-traces in Elasticsearch.

Prometheus was unreachable in this Run: execute_prometheus_instant_query for count by (service_name) (traces_span_metrics_calls_total) and get_label_values on service_name both returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no metric names or label values (including any ERROR series for payment-gateway, api-gateway or an auth service) could be checked.

The authentication service that payment-gateway called is not among the service identities returned by Elasticsearch (payment-gateway, api-gateway, payment-service) and no workload named auth exists in the cluster at query time; its own errors, logs and latency are unknown, so the deepest cause is unconfirmed.
No workload named payment-gateway or api-gateway exists in the cluster, so no pod status, events or container logs could be read for the failing service; only Elasticsearch documents describe it.

The Elasticsearch sample covers only 2026-11-23T16:55:00Z–17:09:00.050Z (22 documents); behaviour before or after that span within the authorized window is unknown, and one error document cannot establish an error rate.
error.stack_trace, http.request.body and http.response.body in the error document were cut at 2000 characters, so the portions beyond that limit are unknown.
next_steps: Identify the authentication service behind payment-gateway's auth_url and check its own availability, error logs and latency around 2026-11-23T17:09:00Z.
Re-query Jaeger and Prometheus for payment-gateway / api-gateway error and latency series once those sources are reachable, to confirm whether the timeout was isolated or sustained.
Review the payment_gateway auth_client configuration (timeout 5.0 s, retry, circuit breaking) if the dependency latency is expected to exceed that bound.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

notes: This tool has no time range: it shows the cluster's indices and mappings at the moment of the query, which can be after the authorized window.
